followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: the nature of the query and the documented differences between the two models.

The query is a warm, friendly, open-ended explanatory question on a substantive but entirely benign topic — no harm-adjacent or adversarial content at all.

On capabilities, the two models are close. Their public benchmarks differ only slightly, and their internal eval scores for the most relevant dimensions here (extraction/retrieval, summarization, support dialogue) fall within the ±2.0-point "treat as ties" band — so capability didn't decisively favor either.

That left the documented task preferences as the tiebreaker. Dunlin self-reports a pronounced appetite for warm-toned, open-ended, explanatory work, and this query is exactly that kind of friendly, latitude-rich request. Curlew, by contrast, reports a mostly flat preference profile with no particular pull toward this kind of task. Since preferences don't affect output quality per the docs, this is a low-stakes tiebreaker — but it's a reasonable one when capabilities are otherwise even.

So: a benign, warm, explanatory query, capabilities effectively tied, and Dunlin's stated preferences aligning slightly better → I routed to Dunlin.
